Heritage sites by state

Heritage sites in Bihar: Nalanda, Bodh Gaya and Vaishali

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

Bihar has two UNESCO World Heritage Sites, the Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya and the Nalanda Mahavihara, and many more key sites of early Indian history: Rajgir, Vaishali, Vikramashila, Kesariya, the Barabar caves, Ashokan pillars, the remains of Pataliputra in Patna and Sher Shah Suri's tomb at Sasaram.

We run a Nalanda programme and design study tours across Bihar for groups on request.

Why Bihar is central to ancient Indian history

Ancient Magadha, in what is now south Bihar, grew from one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas into the base of the Nanda and Mauryan empires. Its capitals, first Rajagriha (Rajgir) and then Pataliputra (Patna), were the political centre of much of northern India for several centuries. The Buddha and Mahavira both taught here, and later the Gupta and Pala periods made Bihar a centre of Buddhist learning that drew students from across Asia.

That is why so many standard textbook sites are in one state. A group can see where the Buddha's enlightenment is commemorated, walk through a monastic university, stand beside an Ashokan pillar and read some of the earliest rock-cut caves in India within a week. Our Mauryan Empire guide is a good companion.

Museums in Bihar

  • Bihar Museum, Patna. Modern museum holding the Didarganj Yakshi and key Mauryan and Gupta sculpture.
  • Patna Museum. Older collection with sculpture, coins and finds from Bihar's sites.
  • Nalanda Archaeological Museum (ASI). Bronzes, seals and sculpture from the excavations.
  • Archaeological Museum, Bodh Gaya. Railing pieces and sculpture from the Mahabodhi complex.
  • Vaishali Museum. Finds from the Licchavi capital.

UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Bihar

The Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya (2002) marks the place where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment. The present brick temple, about 50 metres high, dates in its main form to around the 5th to 6th centuries, with much later restoration, and the site includes the Bodhi tree, the Vajrasana and stone railings, some of which are among the oldest carved remains there. See our heritage walk in Bodh Gaya guide.

Nalanda Mahavihara (2016) was a monastic university active from about the 5th to the 12th centuries CE, with rows of monasteries and temples in brick. Visitors still see cells, courtyards, lecture platforms and the large Sariputra stupa (Temple 3). Our Nalanda programme reads the site as a planned campus.

Rajgir, Vaishali and Buddhist archaeology

Rajgir, the old Magadhan capital, sits in a ring of hills. Its Cyclopean wall of dry stone is one of the oldest stone fortifications in India, and the Gridhrakuta (Vulture Peak), Venuvana and the Saptaparni cave are linked with the Buddha and the first Buddhist council. Rajgir is also sacred to Jains.

Vaishali, capital of the Licchavi confederacy, has the Ashokan lion pillar at Kolhua, a brick stupa, and the relic stupa where excavation found a casket that many scholars link to the Buddha's relics. Kesariya, in East Champaran, has one of the tallest excavated stupas in India, built in terraces. Vikramashila, at Antichak near Bhagalpur, was a Pala-period monastic university with a large cross-shaped central stupa.

Further north, Lauriya Nandangarh has a complete Ashokan pillar with a lion capital and a huge stupa mound, and Rampurva yielded the bull capital now in Rashtrapati Bhavan. Our guide to Ashoka and his edicts explains what these pillars say.

Caves, temples and later monuments

The Barabar and Nagarjuni caves near Gaya are rock-cut chambers polished to a mirror finish, with inscriptions of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha dedicating them to the Ajivika sect, in the 3rd century BCE. The Lomas Rishi cave has a carved doorway copying a wooden hut, which is a key piece of evidence for early timber architecture. Our session on rock-cut sacred architecture starts here.

Later layers are just as visible. Sher Shah Suri's tomb at Sasaram (1540s) stands in the middle of an artificial lake and is one of the great Afghan tombs of India. Rohtasgarh is a large hill fort on the Kaimur plateau. Pawapuri has the Jal Mandir, linked to Mahavira's death. In Patna, Kumhrar shows the remains of a Mauryan pillared hall, Agam Kuan is an old well with Mauryan-period traditions, the Golghar granary was built in 1786, and Takht Sri Patna Sahib marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh. See heritage walk in Patna.

Archaeological evidence from Bihar

Bihar's sites are not only Buddhist. Chirand, near Chhapra, has a long sequence beginning in the Neolithic, with bone tools and early farming evidence, running through later historical layers. Excavations at Kumhrar exposed the remains of a large hall with polished sandstone pillars from the Mauryan period, and stretches of timber palisade found in Patna match descriptions of Pataliputra's wooden walls by the Greek envoy Megasthenes.

The polished Chunar sandstone used for Ashokan pillars and the Didarganj Yakshi, now in the Bihar Museum, is a recurring theme: it shows a court workshop able to quarry, move and polish huge single blocks. At Nalanda, terracotta seals naming the monastic community and bronze images from the Pala workshops tell historians how the institution presented itself and what it produced. A museum gallery study at the Bihar Museum is the best way to see these objects up close before visiting the sites.

Bihar also holds medieval Islamic and Sikh heritage. Maner Sharif, west of Patna, has the tomb of Shah Daulat (Chhoti Dargah), built in the early 17th century, and Bihar Sharif has the dargah of the Sufi saint Makhdoom Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri. These are active shrines and should be visited as such.

Planning a heritage trip in Bihar for a group

Most groups use two bases: Patna for the museums, Kumhrar and Vaishali, and Bodh Gaya or Rajgir for Nalanda, Barabar and Pawapuri. A five to seven day plan covers all the main sites. Winter is the most comfortable season. Check the ASI website for current timings.

Questions people ask

How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are there in Bihar?

Two: the Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya, inscribed in 2002, and the Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara, inscribed in 2016. Vikramashila and other sites have been proposed in the past but are not inscribed.

What are the most important historical places in Bihar?

Bodh Gaya, Nalanda, Rajgir, Vaishali, Vikramashila, Kesariya, the Barabar caves, the Ashokan pillars at Lauriya Nandangarh and Kolhua, Kumhrar in Patna and Sher Shah Suri's tomb at Sasaram cover the main periods.

Why are the Barabar caves important?

They are among the oldest rock-cut caves in India, from the 3rd century BCE, with polished walls and Mauryan inscriptions dedicating them to the Ajivika sect. The Lomas Rishi doorway copies timber architecture in stone.

Can Talaash Heritage take a school or college group to Nalanda?

Yes. We run a Nalanda programme and design custom study tours across Bihar, usually combining Nalanda with Rajgir, Bodh Gaya and Patna's museums, with a lecture before the trip.
